newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot gas prices rise, exports soar in week.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot gas prices rise, exports soar in week.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices climbed from last week in Wednesday trade with export points following NYMEX and U.S. prices skyward.

Spot gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was quoted at C$2.06/2.065 per gigajoule, up from from C$1.87/1.89 last week, as western Canadian weather was forecast to turn frigid by the weekend. Gas for January delivery was talked at C$2.18/2.20 per GJ, up from C$2.08/2.10 on December 11.
Traders said 1.5 billion cubic feet per day was withdrawn from Alberta storage Tuesday, but NOVA's pipeline line pack was still down by 100 million cubic feet per day.
"If we do get a gold snap, storage probably won't be enough to crush the price," said a Calgary-based marketer.

Meanwhile, all border points traded up sharply from last week. Gas at Sumas on the west coast was talked between US$4.23 and US$4.30 per million British thermal units, up about US$1.50 on the week. Temperatures were forecast to drop considerably by the weekend and traders noted there were very few trading days left until the end of the month.

Gas at Niagara was discussed as high as US$4.37 permmBtu, also up about US$1.50 over last week. Cold U.S. weather was the main factor behind the surge, marketers said. ((-- Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
